notes.reason: The author is asking one narrow question: when Dario Amodei wrote that there must be "protective measures against political favoritism or arbitrary decisions", did he ever mean something beyond the courts? His sentence is "Anthropic has never, to my knowledge, proposed that anyone working in AI should have new or different protections from the government than the ordinary course of the law", and in that paragraph "protections from the government" plainly means shields against government action, not employment rights granted by a statute. The note answers with SB 53's whistleblower clause, and I checked Anthropic's endorsement page and the bill coverage: those protections stop a frontier AI developer from retaliating against its own employees who report catastrophic risk, so they protect workers from their employer, not from the government. That is a different subject from the one the author raises, so the note does not actually contradict him. The note also never states what it is correcting, it just reports that Anthropic endorsed SB 53, so a reader would not come away with any changed belief about the argument. On top of that the extracted claim drops the author's own hedge "to my knowledge", which makes his sentence sound like a flat historical assertion it never was. This is the exact failure mode Andy Masley complained about, and the author, who is writing a pointed critique of Anthropic, would read it as a non-sequitur.
